name: New Mexico Eats: Red or Green
subtitle: Green Chile, Burritos & More
description:
New Mexico's restaurants, from a green chile cheeseburger at an old highway bar to a breakfast burrito smothered Christmas.

New Mexico Eats is a free guide to eating in New Mexico: 34 green chile cheeseburger stops, 25 breakfast burrito stops and 25 long-running family restaurants we checked by hand, plus 4,097 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 154 towns, from Albuquerque and Santa Fe to Las Cruces, Farmington and the Eastern Plains. No account, no ads.

NEW MEXICO GUIDES
• Green Chile Cheeseburgers: stops on New Mexico True's trail, from San Antonio to Hatch and Gallup.
• Breakfast Burritos: stops on New Mexico True's byway, red, green or Christmas.
• Culinary Treasures: family restaurants that have stood the test of time.
• Oldest Places: 3 restaurants with a checked founding year.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: 27 honored New Mexico restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "green chile cheeseburger", "burrito santa fe", "sopaipillas".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against New Mexico True's own trails (the state tourism department) or a dated 2025 or 2026 source, matched to an open listing at its address. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested where cities publish official restaurant lists. Albuquerque publishes a weekly report of its restaurant inspections; Albuquerque places show the result they have posted (Approved, Conditional Approved, Unsatisfactory or Closed) as the city words it, dated. Elsewhere the Environment Department and Bernalillo County publish no results online, so each place links the program. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the New Mexico Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of New Mexico, the New Mexico Tourism Department or New Mexico True, the Environment Department, or any city, county or Pueblo), or with Michelin or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: New Mexico Eats is a free guide to restaurants in New Mexico (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: green chile cheeseburgers, breakfast burritos and long-running family restaurants, 82 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against the state tourism department's own trails, plus the MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 4,097 restaurants, cafés and bars in 154 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Green Chile Cheeseburgers (or Breakfast Burritos, Culinary Treasures, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; on Albuquerque places a "Health inspections" section shows the result the city has posted, as the city words it, with its date, and a link opens the city's inspection page in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("green chile cheeseburger", "burrito santa fe", "sopaipillas").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside New Mexico (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on New Mexico, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "New Mexico Eats" is the Home Screen name of "New Mexico Eats: Red or Green".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the New Mexico Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the City of Albuquerque's weekly inspection reports (public records); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites and New Mexico True's trail listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/new-mexico-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers New Mexico; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Official inspection results are shown only as the city publishes them, labeled and dated; the app computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or award body.
